references.phrase: derivative function on an open interval

references.context: Real analysis/topology: open interval I⊆ℝ, possibly unbounded, such that for each x∈I there exists δ>0 with (x−δ,x+δ)⊆I; each point is interior to the real domain.
references.reason: The source differentiates at every point of an open real interval, not at arbitrary boundary points of an interval.
references.matching_note: Check against open subsets of ℝ and open interval candidates in global audit, not against abstract arbitrary intervals without topology.

references.disposition: Equality for every x in I between derivative values F′(x) and f(x) is exactly the predicate defining an antiderivative; the derivative and derivative-function notions are linked separately.
If one exists, adding real constants gives others; equality of the derivative alone does not select a unique F.

references.phrase: antiderivative F of f on I

references.disposition: The displayed set of additive translates F+C is the actual object designated by this formulation of the indefinite integral, not a separate prerequisite definition; function addition and constants are ordinary operations in this context.

references.context: Real analysis: constant real-valued function c_I:I→ℝ mapping all x∈I to a fixed C∈ℝ, added pointwise to a differentiable function F; derivative of the constant function is zero.
references.reason: The notation F+C presupposes the constant-function construction, not a single special value of the definite integral.
references.matching_note: Avoid conflating integration constant as scalar parameter with a distinct fixed antiderivative.

references.phrase: symbol indefinite integral does not denote a single number
references.disposition: It denotes a family of functions, not a definite integral over an interval.

references.context: Single-variable real analysis: difference quotient Q(h)=[f(a+h)−f(a)]/h for h≠0 with a,a+h in the domain of f; interpreted as a function of punctured nonzero increments h.
references.reason: The difference quotient is a reusable construction preceding its limit, which defines the derivative.
references.matching_note: This is an ordinary real difference quotient, not a partial derivative, metric slope of a curve, or differential in a normed vector space.
The finite real limit of the difference quotient function as its real input h approaches 0 through nonzero increments is exactly the indexed punctured-limit concept; no value at h=0 is required.

references.disposition: Derivative is defined only if the difference quotient approaches a finite real number.

references.context: Real topology: deleted δ-neighborhood {x∈ℝ:0<|x−a|<δ} of a, intersected with the function domain; the center a itself is excluded.
references.reason: The punctured neighborhood is a reusable domain restriction and is not the same thing as requiring continuity at a.
references.matching_note: Check against general topological punctured neighborhoods, preserving real metric interval context.

references.disposition: The ∀ε>0 ∃δ>0 ∀x implication is the defining logical predicate of a finite real limit; it is not a separately required notion of epsilon-delta continuity. Real ordering/absolute value are already linked.
Only punctured domain values are used, so the value at a need not exist or equal L.

references.context: Real linear algebra: bilinear map B:V×V→ℝ linear separately in each vector argument and symmetric B(u,v)=B(v,u); distinct from a complex Hermitian sesquilinear form.
references.reason: Real inner-product-space structure presupposes the bilinear and symmetric properties as reusable algebraic prerequisites.
references.matching_note: Compare globally with module bilinear-map context; field ℝ and symmetry should not be lost.

references.context: Real linear algebra: positive-definiteness of a symmetric bilinear form B on real V, with B(v,v)>0 for all nonzero v∈V and B(0,0)=0.
references.reason: Positive definiteness is an independently meaningful predicate on forms, not supplied automatically by symmetry or bilinearity.
references.matching_note: Do not confuse with semidefinite forms (which permit nonzero vectors with zero self-pairing).

references.phrase: real rather than complex Hermitian convention
references.disposition: No conjugate-linear component in the real bilinear form definition.
